Key facts so far:
- Validate X-Hub-Signature-256, HMAC-SHA256 with secret, over raw payload body, constant-time compare; never plain ==. Re-serializing JSON breaks the signature — must verify over the original raw bytes.
- Respond 2XX within 10 seconds; GitHub terminates connection and considers delivery a failure otherwise. So a 25-second job must be enqueued async; respond immediately after verification+enqueue (e.g., 202).
- Best practices: "Redeliver missed deliveries": if server goes down, you should redeliver missed webhooks once back up — so automatic retry after outage is NOT documented; recovery is manual/scripted redelivery. Need to check "automatically redelivering failed deliveries for a repository webhook" — script to auto-redeliver failed deliveries; also the redelivering-webhooks page in testing-and-troubleshooting. Key note: "If you request a redelivery, the X-GitHub-Delivery header will be the same as in the original delivery." — this corrects the team's premise.
- X-GitHub-Delivery header: unique per event; use to protect against replay attacks (dedup).

Still needed: delivery headers page (X-GitHub-Delivery GUID in webhook events and payloads) and the automatically-redelivering page to see retry semantics and whether deliveries are considered failed after 10s and whether GitHub auto-retries (docs say for GitHub App webhooks... "Automatically redelivering failed deliveries" is about a script you write to redeliver failed deliveries — not automatic server-side retry). Also "Redelivering webhooks" page. Let me fetch the automatically-redelivering-failed-deliveries-for-a-repository-webhook page and the redelivering-webhooks page. That's turn 3 with two fetches.
